WoW: Forever

Camping

New in Forever. A cook lights a fire, everyone drops one crafted object beside it, and the whole group carries the buffs for an hour, including buffs that normally need a specific class.

WoW: Forever · System · Updated October 8, 2026 · Beta build 1.60.1.70245 · Null Ossuary

Camp objects, skill levels and buff values come from foreverchanges.pro's reading of the beta client and are solid. Several mechanics are genuinely unsettled: whether camps work in cities and instances, whether you must be grouped to receive someone else's buff, and where each Blueprint drops. Blizzard's own panel and the beta client also disagree on two numbers, flagged below.

On this page

  • How camping works
  • What each profession brings
  • Campfire capacity
  • Two published numbers that disagree
  • What changed in the October 1 build
  • What is not known

How camping works

  1. A cook places a campfire. Basic Campfire KitBasic Campfire KitItem takes 1 Simple Wood and Flint and Tinder. It burns 15 minutes, and no other campfire can be within 100 yards
  2. Each player adds one object from their own profession, learned at skill 20
  3. Wait a minute at the fire. Since the September 24 build, sitting, sitting in a chair, sleeping, lying down and the kneeling emote all count. You may buff, cast and craft while you wait
  4. The buffs last an hour, and you can then walk away

Camp objects share a one-hour cooldown. You set a camp up before a session, not between pulls.

Objects are tradeable, but placing one needs the skill. You cannot buy your way to a full camp.

What each profession brings

Every profession has three objects, at skill 20, 140 and 300. The 140 and 300 ones come from Blueprints that drop from dungeon bosses, and each replacement keeps the buff of the object it replaces.

Every object, value and non-stacking rule in that table is foreverchanges.pro's reading of the client. Blizzard describes camping itself, names the campfire and the Boosted RestBoosted RestSpell · PhysicalCastInstantDuration3600 sec debuff, and has rewritten its tooltips. It has published no camp object, no buff value and no equivalence to a class buff.

Every stat buff in that table is the figure at the level beside it, and the client scales the rest by character level. Each object climbs on its own ladder: the Lodestone pays 12 attack power below level 12, then 20, 32, 49 and 67, before reaching 90 at 52. At the beta's level-30 cap a full camp hands out 32 attack power, 12 Intellect, 21 Stamina and 15 mana every 5 seconds. Add 11 Strength, 14 Spirit, and the Lute's 163 armour with +7 all stats and +6 all resistances. The three percentage buffs do not scale: the Fish Bowl's 8%, the Camp Chair's 2% and the Camp Tent's 5% read the same at every level.

A camp hands a group the class buffs it does not have. A party with no Paladin can still have Blessing of Kings, Might and Wisdom. None of them stacks with the real thing, so you get one or the other. The Druid crit aura appears twice because Blizzard made Moonkin FormMoonkin FormLevel 40 · Spell · PhysicalCastInstantDurationUntil cancelledShapeshift into Moonkin Form, increasing Omen of Clarity's chance to trigger by 100%, Armor contribution from items by 360%, and all party members within 45 yards have their Critical Strike chance increased by 3%, exclusive with Leader of the Pack. Also protects the caster from Polymorph effects and prevents the use of healing spells. The act of shapeshifting frees the caster of Polymorph and Movement Impairing effects. and Leader of the PackLeader of the PackSpell · PhysicalCastInstantWhile in Cat Form, Bear Form, or Dire Bear Form, the Leader of the Pack increases the critical strike chance of all party members within 45 yards by 3%, exclusive with Moonkin Aura. the same effect, mutually exclusive with each other.

The Camp TentCamp TentItem tops up rather than stacks: "does nothing if you already have more." The Faction BannerFaction BannerItem only buffs your own faction, and has separate Horde and Alliance recipes.

You can learn a Blueprint well before you can craft the kit, which is why guides quote different numbers for the same thing. Both are right, printed from different columns.

Two published numbers that disagree

  • The Sharpening WheelSharpening WheelItem is widely reported as giving attack power. The beta client says Strength. The client is what is live, and both guide sites follow it. The attack-power claim is attributed to Blizzard's What's Next panel, but the recap this page cites does not contain it, so treat it as reported rather than published.
  • A basic campfire is likewise reported as allowing three objects. The client shows 3, 5 and 10 for the three kit tiers, so that reading fits the basic kit only — and again, the cited recap does not say it.

What changed in the October 1 build

  • Campfires no longer damage players below level 5, and they deal reduced damage to players under 90% health.
  • The Boosted RestBoosted RestSpell · PhysicalCastInstantDuration3600 sec debuff has a new icon and a rewritten tooltip, which Blizzard says is "intended to make the effect clearer." No value changed. Leatherworking's Camp TentCamp TentItem is the only rest-related camp object on this page. Blizzard's note names the debuff but not the object it belongs to, so that link is inferred here rather than stated.
  • Camping tooltips now say "mutually exclusive" instead of just "exclusive", which Blizzard did "to reduce some confusion around functionality." This page describes effects as not stacking, so nothing above needed correcting. Four profession pages did: the camp-object tables on Alchemy, First Aid, Herbalism and Mining each read "Exclusive with", and all four now carry Blizzard's term.

What is not known

Whether camps function in cities and in instances. Whether you must be grouped to receive another player's buff, which nobody has answered. How many objects one craft produces. And where each of the 140 and 300 Blueprints drops, beyond "specific dungeon bosses". Two are known: Alchemy's FermenterFermenterItem Blueprint drops in Wailing Caverns and Ruins of Lordaeron.

Sources

Compiled from the three major Forever guide sites and cross-checked against each other. Where Blizzard has published an official class deep dive, that post outranks all three and the page is written from it. Everything else — talent ranks, tooltip values, what exists in the tree at all — is settled against the client itself, read through foreverchanges.pro and wago.tools. Where the guides disagree with each other, this page says which said what.
